sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This appeal has been filed by the third respondent insurer in OP(MV) No.1132 of 2012 on the file of the III Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam, challenging the impugned award dated 21.05.2014.

entities.text: III Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents herein were the claimants before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimants before the tribunal was that on 06.10.2011, while the deceased was riding a motorcycle, a bus bearing Reg.No.KL-07/BE-1004 driven by the second respondent, hit behind the motorcycle, whereby he sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the way to hospital.
The claimants, being the legal heirs of the deceased, approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 10,00,000/-.
Respondents 1 and 2 remained ex parte before the tribunal.
The respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy coverage for the offending vehicle, but disputing the liability and quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A15 were marked on the side of the claimants.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record,
held that the 2025:KER:40333 ..3..
accident took place on account of the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and awarded a sum of 16,61,468/- as compensation under different heads against the third respondent being the insurer.
3.

The appeal is filed by the insurer challenging the impugned award mainly on two grounds; firstly,
regarding the split multiplier adopted and secondly, the proportionate costs awarded.
4. Today, when the case was taken up, the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant insurer submits that the insurer is not pressing the first challenge regarding application of split multiplier.
As regards the second ground, the learned Standing Counsel submits that for the awarded compensation of 16,61,468/-, the total advocate fee payable was 85,373/- as per the Advocates Act, 1961.
5. On a perusal of the impugned award and on calculating the same as per the Advocates Act, 1961, I find that the amount to be awarded towards proportionate costs is only 85,373/-.
No Junior Advocate fee is also payable in this case since there was no vakalath filed by the junior lawyer.

The amount of 8,10,634/- awarded towards Senior Advocate fee and the amount of 28,491/- awarded towards Junior Advocate fee by the tribunal as proportionate costs is on the higher side and is to be interfered with.
Hence, I deem it appropriate to refix the Advocate fee at 85,373/-.
